mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are revised downwards.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the GDP growth is negative, or if the correlation between GDP declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% within the last two months signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic activity and corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts and a decrease in retail sales signal a shift in consumer spending from goods to housing, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market participants reassess economic fundamentals.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increase > 5% and RSAFS decrease > 1% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls by more than 100,000 in the last month signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending decline.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between PAYEMS declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the consumer price index by more than 0.5% within the last month signals rising inflation, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded and the Fed is expected to tighten monetary policy.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between CPIAUCSL increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP growth over two consecutive quarters signals a strengthening demand environment, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are revised upwards.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where the GDP growth is positive, or if the correlation between GDP increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
